---
title: "Why representation bias matters"
---

Digital mobility data describe the people observed by a provider. Their
geographical distribution can differ from the population whose travel patterns
we want to estimate. Adjustments use coverage, benchmark flows or modelled
relationships to account for those differences.

Start by defining the counting unit and population of interest. Then measure
coverage, choose an adjustment supported by the available data, and compare
its results with a suitable benchmark. A benchmark used for calibration also
influences the adjustment; independent evaluation is needed to assess accuracy
beyond that calibration data.

The Census example demonstrates the workflow. The public functions also accept
other OD and benchmark tables that meet the [input definitions](../inputs.md).
